note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect and until is derived by hand from the 16-wire topology and the Books V-VI p.56 rule, not printed. Wires are the printed 16 unchanged (no erratum). Topology: pushbutton 1's arm 1Y is on +; 1Z/6Z and 1X/6X carry it to pushbutton 6's matching contact, and 6Y feeds relay 6's coil (6E/6Y, 6F/6-), so relay 6 is in exactly when pushbuttons 1 and 6 are in the same position. Relay 6 out: 6H(+)-6J puts + on D17 and 6L(-)-6N puts - on D18 (normal RUN, increasing numbers, clockwise). Relay 6 in: 6H-6G-6N puts + on D18 and 6L-6K-6J puts - on D17 (reversed, decreasing, counterclockwise). Pushbutton 4 up (4Y-4Z) ties D18 to the D7-D8-D9 strap and D16/D19 ties the wiper to D19, so STOP is shorted on 7, 8 or 9; play runs over 10-15 and 0-6, 9 is entered from 10 and 7 from 6. No lamp terminal is wired, so all twelve lamps stay dark. Script choices, not printed: power-on dial c0 (construction state, both buttons up, so the power-on run rests on 9); pushbutton 4 released as soon as the dial leaves its rest contact (p.57 'Release pushbutton 4 as the rotary switch knob starts to turn'), except game 2; 100 ms after a player button change before the hold-on-the-arc expects; 10 s settles before each end expect. Game 1: different from 9 (pb1 up, pb6 down), dial asserted on 10 after the re-set (clockwise), player 1 tugs (pb1 down) when the dial reaches 3, then contact 2 proves the reversal, end on 9. Game 2 is the O-R16 crossing case: same from rest on 9 with pushbutton 4 held until the wiper reaches 6, then released; the derived end is 9. A prompt release on that crossing would let the restored STOP short catch the wiper on 8, which the topology also predicts; that depends on the human's hold and is not asserted. Game 3: different with pb1 down, pb6 up, end on 7. Game 4: same with both up from rest on 7, dial asserted on 6 after the re-set (counterclockwise), player 2 tugs (pb6 down) at 13, contact 14 proves the reversal, end on 7. All four button combinations are exercised. The position-triggered tugs replace the printed fixture's fixed 770 ms tug, so this fixture holds at any run rate; the untils allow 15 s, the end settles 10 s (over a full revolution down to about 7 rpm). Relies on the stop-shorted coast staying inside the contact arc (O-R5). The digest is a placeholder for the runner.
